findings.evidence: A lane marked `usage_limited = true` is probed like any other. ... this check passes a throwaway `--quota-path`, so every `--check-only` run spends one probe per probed lane, including part of a usage-limited lane's allowance.
findings.fix: State that probe-quota still selects usage-limited lanes, but that execute selection uses the fallback order: the review order first, then execute lanes that are neither usage-limited nor in the same pool, then the rest. A usage-limited execute lane is not probed when an unflagged lane outside its pool exists.

findings.evidence: Today only Claude Code selects a model per call (its sonnet, opus, haiku and fable aliases); every other host runs only its session default natively.
findings.fix: Give the selectors in the order the runtime table stores them, fable, opus, sonnet, haiku, and say that list is the table's native_selectors, not a claim about Claude Code's full alias set.

findings.evidence: the first `default_view` rows of `pool`, each with its rank, key, runtime, class, cost band, price and `ranker_reason`
findings.fix: Name the printed fields: rank, key, runtime, model_id, class (the JSON also repeats it as class_label), cost_band, price and ranker_reason, and say default_view is the integer 12.

Run one report: --detect when this run needs a live listing to prove staleness, otherwise the saved snapshot. Say the two flags are mutually exclusive and that attribution is printed only when the catalog records a known source.

findings.evidence: The 21 cases assert that named commands run and that answers are respected, but none checks the JSON or TOML the agent must hand render-toml, such as purpose both, a session-default entry with no runtime and model empty, or data_use unknown with source none.
findings.fix: Add assertions that quote the lane object the agent writes for those three cases, and add three negative queries for a neighbour: sorting skills alone, trusting an already written roster, and probing quota without the check-only setup.

findings.evidence: The description names review and execute lanes, --check-only, --local, --global and review-spec.toml, and excludes running a review, hand-editing one lane and editing [runner] or opencode.jsonc.
findings.fix: Cross-AI lane setup: detect installed CLIs and models, propose a review set and an execute set from the model catalog, ask each role's order, effort and opt-in flags, and write the [lanes] table of .aikit/config.toml or the user ai-kit config.toml. Use when the user wants to set up, refresh or check cross-AI review or execute lanes, even without the word lanes; when no lanes exist; to find lane providers opencode no longer lists; or to ask about migrating review-spec.toml. Supports --check-only, --local and --global. Not for running a review or execute with configured lanes, hand-editing one lane, editing [runner] or opencode.jsonc, or writing a skill role without a lane setup.

findings.evidence: escalate_runtime and escalate_model are stored opt-in flags ... no run reads them yet.
findings.fix: Keep the stored-not-consumed statement, and add the real reader rule beside it: a usage-limited lane's fallback is the first lane of its role that is neither usage-limited nor in the same pool, and execute selection already uses that order.

findings.evidence: Before registering any lane, weigh two judgment calls ... the proposal ranks per purpose.
findings.fix: Move those two questions into wizard-flow.md step 3, where the owner sees the shortlist, and leave SKILL.md's Step 2 table as routing only.
